item.title: (News) India's Supreme Court questions electoral commission independence
item.description:
Source: Supreme Court asks if there was a 'proper debate' in Parliament before enacting CEC/EC appointments law

India's Supreme Court is examining the independence of the Election Commission following a 2023 law that increased executive control over appointments. This law replaced the Chief Justice on the selection committee with a minister, raising concerns about democratic safeguards amid parliamentary actions. This highlights the importance of institutional checks and balances in democracies, informing UK/EU professionals about global governance trends.

System Note: While legitimate concerns exist regarding institutional oversight, the judicial questioning reflects functioning democratic processes and scrutiny.

item.title: (Video) Experimenting with bottle deposit schemes inspired by Seinfeld
item.description:
Source: Beau Miles



Inspired by a Seinfeld episode, a creator attempts to collect 10,000 bottles and cans to claim deposits. The video documents the process of gathering and returning containers, exploring the practicalities and challenges of bottle deposit schemes.

item.title: (Research) Exploring the concept of a second Axial Age
item.description:
Source: NOEMA



This article examines the concept of a potential second Axial Age, a period of profound philosophical and societal transformation. It discusses historical parallels and contemporary shifts that suggest humanity is at the cusp of a new era of global consciousness.

item.title: (Research) Microbiome research and the holobiont concept of health
item.description:
Source: Platypus

This article explores how microbiome research challenges traditional views of human health by introducing the holobiont concept. It frames health as a relational and ecological state, influenced by complex interactions between host and microorganisms.

item.title: (Research) Tyler Thier on subjective perception in photography and media
item.description:
Source: Psyche | Know Your Self

Tyler Thier reflects on how personal interpretation shapes perception when observing others through cameras and screens. The essay explores the subjective nature of truth in media, where viewers often fill in narrative gaps with their own biases.

item.title: (Audio) Career discovery through interviews with diverse professionals
item.description:
Source: Time We Discuss



This podcast features discussions and interviews with professionals across various fields, offering insights into daily work life and career paths. It assists listeners in career discovery, job exploration, and making informed decisions about education and professional development.

item.title: (Audio) Stuart McLean's stories of community projects
item.description:
Source: Backstage at the Vinyl Cafe



This episode features Stuart McLean's stories exploring various community ventures, including an inspiring project like The Smiths Falls Station Theatre. It delves into the diverse ways people come together to create local initiatives and shared experiences.

item.title: (Audio) Brian Colburn's podcast on music discovery and cultural memory
item.description:
Source: Brian Colburn



Brian Colburn's podcast explores music discovery and nostalgia through curated playlists, artist interviews, and song stories. It examines how music shapes memory, identity, and personal experiences across various genres, offering track-by-track insights.

item.title: (Video) Lateral reading techniques for media literacy and emotional intelligence
item.description:
Source: Yale Center for Emotional Intelligence



This video introduces lateral reading as a practical method to enhance media literacy and emotional intelligence. It demonstrates how to verify information by consulting multiple sources, fostering critical thinking and informed judgment.

item.title: (Video) Professor Sir Martyn Poliakoff examines unusual laboratory glassware
item.description:
Source: Periodic Videos



Professor Sir Martyn Poliakoff from the Periodic Table of Videos series investigates unique glassware found in a storeroom. He explores the potential origins, purposes, and chemical significance of these unusual laboratory items.

item.title: (Video) New methods to repurpose tire waste
item.description:
Source: AsapSCIENCE



Researchers explore innovative substances and processes to prevent billions of used tires from becoming environmental waste. The initiative seeks to develop new applications for discarded tires, moving towards a circular economy for rubber products.

item.title: (Video) Professor Sebastian Ruth on music as a tool for social action
item.description:
Source: YaleCourses



Professor Sebastian Ruth presents a Yale Online webinar exploring the intersection of music and social action. The discussion examines how musical engagement can serve as a catalyst for community building and positive societal change.

item.title: (Video) Craig Newmark's approach to Craigslist and open internet principles
item.description:
Source: Conversations with Tyler



Craig Newmark discusses his career maintaining Craigslist's simplicity and his advocacy for an open, decentralized internet. He explores principles of institutional control, the evolution of online platforms, and the importance of ceding power.
